2027-06-05.title: Third Saturday of the Apostles: the Feast of the Immaculate Heart of Mary
2027-06-05.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: Sarah shall give rise to nations
The Lord himself will give you a sign: Immanuel
Chosen in Christ to be holy and blameless

2027-06-05.alt: Season of the Apostles (Šleehe), from Pentecost to the beginning of the Season of Summer (Kaitha): the Church remembers the apostles who, filled with the Holy Spirit, preached Christ and founded the Churches, among them the Church of India founded by Mar Thoma. The Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Addai and Mari, and the Angel of the Lord (Angelus) is prayed at the three hours of the day. The Immaculate Heart of Mary is listed in the First Set calendar as an important Marian feast; no seasonal readings are printed for the Third Saturday, so the feast's readings are the day's. In the Latin calendar the memorial of the Immaculate Heart falls this year on the same day as that of St Boniface, bishop and martyr, and both are optional. 5 June is also World Environment Day.
2027-06-05.verse: Then he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was obedient to them. His mother treasured all these things in her heart.
theo: Yesterday the Church looked on the pierced Heart of Jesus; today she turns to the Heart of his Mother. The two belong together. When the infant Jesus was presented in the Temple, old Simeon said to Mary, “and a sword will pierce your own soul too” (Luke 2:35), and at the foot of the Cross that sword went through her heart as the spear went through his. The devotion to the Heart of Mary is old in the Church. St John Eudes in the seventeenth century gave it a liturgical form; at Fatima in 1917 the Mother of God spoke to three shepherd children of her Immaculate Heart; Pope Pius XII consecrated the world to the Immaculate Heart in 1942 and extended the feast to the whole Church in 1944, and Pope Francis renewed the consecration of humanity, and in particular of Russia and Ukraine, on 25 March 2022. The word Immaculate reminds us that this heart was never stained by sin. By a singular grace and in view of the merits of Christ, Mary was preserved from original sin from the first moment of her conception. The word Heart reminds us of her inner life: the place where she received the word of God, kept it, pondered it and answered it with her whole self. In the Syro-Malabar calendar this is an important Marian feast, and it falls fittingly in the Season of the Apostles, for after the Ascension the apostles “were constantly devoting themselves to prayer, together with certain women, including Mary the mother of Jesus” (Acts 1:14). The first Church was gathered around the heart of the Mother.

The first reading is God's promise to Abraham about his wife: “As for Sarai your wife, you shall not call her Sarai, but Sarah shall be her name. I will bless her, and moreover I will give you a son by her. I will bless her, and she shall give rise to nations; kings of peoples shall come from her.” Abraham falls on his face and laughs: “Can a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old? Can Sarah, who is ninety years old, bear a child?” God holds to his word: Sarah will bear Isaac, and the everlasting covenant will pass through him. God does not forget Ishmael either: “As for Ishmael, I have heard you; I will bless him.” The Church reads this passage today because Sarah, the barren woman who becomes a mother of nations by God's power, is a figure of the Mother of the Messiah. What God began with Sarah's laughter he completed in Mary's faith. To her the angel said what was said to Abraham long before: “For nothing will be impossible with God” (Luke 1:37). Mary became the mother not of one nation but of all, for from the Cross Jesus gave her to the beloved disciple and, through him, to the whole Church: “Here is your mother” (John 19:27).

In the second reading King Ahaz of Judah is terrified because two neighbouring kings have joined against him. The prophet Isaiah invites him to trust God and even to ask for a sign, as deep as Sheol or as high as heaven. Ahaz refuses with pious words, “I will not ask, and I will not put the Lord to the test”, because he has already decided to trust in a foreign empire rather than in God. Isaiah answers: “Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign. Look, the young woman is with child and shall bear a son, and shall name him Immanuel.” The Hebrew word speaks of a young woman of marriageable age; the ancient Greek translation made by Jewish scholars before Christ rendered it “virgin”; and St Matthew, quoting that translation, sees the sign fulfilled in Mary: “Look, the virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and they shall name him Emmanuel,” which means, “God is with us” (Matthew 1:23). The Church professes that Mary conceived by the Holy Spirit without the seed of man and remained a virgin for ever. And notice the contrast between two hearts. Ahaz's heart was closed by fear and calculation; he would not even ask. Mary's heart was open; she asked, “How can this be?”, and then said, “Here am I, the servant of the Lord; let it be with me according to your word” (Luke 1:38).

The Epistle is the great blessing that opens the Letter to the Ephesians: “Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who has blessed us in Christ with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places, just as he chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world to be holy and blameless before him in love.” This is God's plan for the whole Church: to be holy and without blemish. What is promised to all of us, and will be completed only at the end, has already been accomplished in one person. Mary was chosen before the foundation of the world, and from the first moment of her existence she was holy and blameless before God in love. She too was redeemed; Paul's next words apply to her first of all: “In him we have redemption through his blood, the forgiveness of our trespasses, according to the riches of his grace that he lavished on us.” She was redeemed, as the Church says, in a more exalted way: not by being washed from sin but by being preserved from it, through the blood her Son would shed. Her Immaculate Heart is the masterpiece of grace, “to the praise of his glorious grace.” That is why honouring Mary never takes anything from Christ; it praises what his grace can do.

The Gospel is the only story from the hidden years of Jesus. At twelve he goes up with Mary and Joseph to Jerusalem for the Passover and stays behind. For three days they search for him. When they find him in the Temple among the teachers, his mother speaks: “Child, why have you treated us like this? Look, your father and I have been searching for you in great anxiety.” Mary does not hide her pain, and she names Joseph first: your father and I. Jesus answers, “Why were you searching for me? Did you not know that I must be in my Father’s house?” And Luke tells us honestly: “But they did not understand what he said to them.” The Immaculate Heart is not a heart that understood everything at once, nor a heart without anxiety. It is a heart that did not close itself in the dark. “Then he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was obedient to them. His mother treasured all these things in her heart.” She kept what she did not yet understand, and turned it over in prayer until God gave the light. Parents who worry about children growing up and going their own way, mothers who have searched through a long night for a son or daughter, can bring their anxiety to her. And all of us can learn from her the way to hold God's word: not to throw it away when it is hard, but to treasure it, ponder it and wait.
conn: God promises enmity between the serpent and the woman, and between their offspring (Genesis 3:15); the Church sees in the woman the New Eve, and in her offspring Christ, who crushes the power of evil.
“Greetings, favored one! The Lord is with you” (Luke 1:28): the greeting of the angel to one who was already filled with God's favour.
“You are altogether beautiful, my love; there is no flaw in you” (Song of Songs 4:7), applied by the Church's tradition to the Immaculate Mother.
“But Mary treasured all these words and pondered them in her heart” (Luke 2:19).
“and a sword will pierce your own soul too” (Luke 2:35).
“Woman, here is your son… Here is your mother” (John 19:26–27).
“All these were constantly devoting themselves to prayer, together with certain women, including Mary the mother of Jesus” (Acts 1:14).
The woman clothed with the sun.
“A great portent appeared in heaven: a woman clothed with the sun, with the moon under her feet, and on her head a crown of twelve stars” (Revelation 12:1).
altar: Mary's heart received the Word of God, and the Word became flesh in her womb. At every Holy Qurbana the same Word made flesh is placed on the altar and given to us. Let us receive him as she received him, with an open and believing heart.
The Mother who stood by the Cross stands by the altar where the sacrifice of the Cross is made present. In her company let us offer ourselves with Christ to the Father.
outline: The pierced Heart of the Son and the pierced heart of the Mother.
Sarah's laughter and Mary's faith: nothing is impossible with God.

Ahaz's closed heart and Mary's open heart; the virgin mother of Immanuel.
Chosen before the foundation of the world; preserved from sin by the blood of her Son.

live: Each evening this week, before sleeping, recall one thing God has said or done that day, and keep it in your heart.
Pray an act of consecration to the Immaculate Heart of Mary this week, alone or with your family.
Pray the rosary for the world
Pray one decade each day for peace, especially for countries at war, as the Mother of God asked at Fatima.
If you are anxious about a child, a marriage or a decision, entrust it to Mary's heart and ask her to keep it with you.
fathers: You alone, Lord, and your Mother are beautiful in every way; for there is no blemish in you, and no stain in your Mother.

Mary conceived Christ first in her heart by faith, and then in her womb. It was a greater thing for her to be his disciple than to be his mother; she is blessed because she heard the word of God and kept it.

Mary kept all these words in her heart: whatever she heard of the Lord, or saw done by him, she laid up carefully in her memory, comparing it with what she had read in the prophets, so that she might ponder it and later hand it on.
magis: Through the centuries the Church has become ever more aware that Mary, full of grace through God, was redeemed from the moment of her conception; in 1854 Pope Pius IX proclaimed the dogma of the Immaculate Conception.

Mary is redeemed in a more exalted fashion, by reason of the merits of her Son; the Father blessed her more than any other created person in Christ, and chose her before the foundation of the world to be holy and blameless before him in love.
The Church confesses Mary's real and perpetual virginity, even in the act of giving birth to the Son of God made man.

At the finding in the Temple Mary and Joseph did not understand his words, but they accepted them in faith, and Mary kept all these things in her heart during the years Jesus remained hidden in the silence of an ordinary life.
Mary's prayer is revealed at the dawning of the fullness of time; her prayer and that of the Church are marked by the generous offering of her whole being in faith.
Pius XII, Act of Consecration (1942) (in substance)
Queen of the most holy Rosary, help of Christians, refuge of the human race, we entrust and consecrate ourselves, the Church and the whole human race, to your Immaculate Heart.
saints: The Feast of the Immaculate Heart of Mary (Syro-Malabar, an important Marian feast). Latin calendar: the Immaculate Heart and St Boniface (about 675–754), the English Benedictine monk who became the apostle of Germany and archbishop of Mainz, martyred at Dokkum in Frisia on 5 June 754 with his companions; both memorials optional this year.

1–6 June: the third and fourth weeks of the Season of the Apostles. Tue 1: St Justin, martyr. Thu 3: in the Latin calendar, St Charles Lwanga and his companions, the Martyrs of Uganda. Fri 4: the Feast of the Sacred Heart of Jesus (Third Friday of the Apostles), and First Friday. Sat 5: the Feast of the Immaculate Heart of Mary (Third Saturday of the Apostles); in the Latin calendar also St Boniface. Sun 6: Fourth Sunday of the Apostles. June is the month of the Sacred Heart in popular devotion; in Kerala it is also the month the schools reopen and the monsoon rains arrive.
2027-06-05.prayer: God our Father, you prepared a worthy dwelling for your Son in the Immaculate Heart of the Virgin Mary, chosen in Christ before the foundation of the world to be holy and blameless in love. As you gave Sarah a son and gave Ahaz a sign, you gave us Immanuel through the faith of Mary. Give us hearts like hers, open to your word, faithful in anxiety, and treasuring what we do not yet understand. Mother of God and Mother of the Church, as you prayed with the apostles in the Upper Room, pray with us now: keep our families in your heart, bring peace to the nations, and lead us to your Son. Through Christ our Lord, who lives and reigns with you and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.

quick: Genesis: God renames Sarai as Sarah and promises that she will bear a son and give rise to nations.
Isaiah: the Lord himself will give a sign: the young woman shall bear a son and name him Immanuel, fulfilled in the Virgin Mary.
Paul: God chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world to be holy and blameless before him in love.
Luke: after three days Mary and Joseph find Jesus in the Temple; his mother treasured all these things in her heart.
2027-06-05.action: Pray an act of consecration to the Immaculate Heart of Mary, and one decade of the rosary each day for peace.
2027-06-05.question: Do I keep God's word in my heart even when I do not understand it?
catechism: Redeemed in a more exalted fashion.
kidsaint: Francisco and Jacinta were a brother and sister from a poor family in Fatima, in Portugal. In 1917, while they looked after sheep with their cousin Lucia, the Mother of God appeared to them. She spoke of her Immaculate Heart and asked them to pray the rosary every day for peace and for sinners. Francisco loved to sit quietly before the tabernacle to comfort Jesus; Jacinta offered little sacrifices for sinners. Both died young, after an illness, and Pope Francis declared them saints in 2017. Lesson: even children can pray every day for peace in the world!
2027-06-05.special: Feast of the Immaculate Heart of Mary (Syro-Malabar, Third Saturday of the Apostles; an important Marian feast). Latin calendar: the Immaculate Heart of Mary and St Boniface, both optional this year. World Environment Day.
term: The heart of the Virgin Mary, never touched by sin, honoured as the sign of her inner life of faith, love and prayer: the heart that kept and pondered the word of God (Luke 2:19, 51) and was pierced by sorrow at the Cross (Luke 2:35). The devotion was given liturgical form by St John Eudes, spread after the apparitions at Fatima (1917), and the feast was extended to the whole Church by Pius XII in 1944. Malayalam: വിമലഹൃദയം.

family.explain: When Jesus was twelve, he went with Mary and Joseph to Jerusalem for a feast. On the way home they could not find him. They searched for three days and were very worried. At last they found him in the Temple, talking with the teachers. Mary told him how worried they had been. Then Jesus went home with them and obeyed them. Mary kept all these things in her heart. Mary's heart was full of love for God and for Jesus, and she loves us too. We can tell her everything that worries us.
family.intention: We pray for children who are lost or have run away, for their parents, and for peace in the world.
family.ask: Ask: “What worry can our family give to Mother Mary today?”

illus: A mother in Kottayam waited up one monsoon night when her sixteen-year-old son did not come home after a quarrel. His phone was switched off. Her husband drove around the town while she knelt at the family altar with the rosary, and after midnight she simply said, ‘Amma, you also searched for your son for three days. Keep mine in your heart.’ Near dawn the boy came in, soaked and silent; he had spent the night at a friend's house. She wanted to shout at him. Instead she gave him a towel and a cup of tea, and they talked only the next evening. Years later, when he was married with his own children, he told her, ‘That night I expected a fight. You gave me tea. I have never forgotten it.’ She told him that she had learned it from the Mother of God, who kept in her heart what she did not understand.

pm.open: Holy Mary, Mother of God and our Mother, your Immaculate Heart kept the word of God and loved Jesus with a perfect love. Pray with us, as you prayed with the apostles, that the Holy Spirit may fill our hearts. Amen.
share: She shall give rise to nations (Genesis 17:16). How has God done in my life what seemed impossible?
The Lord himself will give you a sign (Isaiah 7:14). Is my heart closed by fear like Ahaz, or open like Mary?
He chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world to be holy and blameless before him in love (Ephesians 1:4). Do I believe that God has chosen me?
His mother treasured all these things in her heart (Luke 2:51). What do I need to keep and ponder, without understanding it yet?
pm.resp: Immaculate Heart of Mary, pray for us.
interc: For the Church, gathered like the apostles around the Mother of Jesus, that she may be filled with the Holy Spirit.
For peace in the world, especially in nations at war, through the intercession of the Immaculate Heart.
For parents anxious about their children, and for children who are lost, that they may be found.
For families, that they may pray the rosary together and keep God's word in their hearts.
For the care of creation on this World Environment Day, that we may protect the earth God has given us.
pm.close: God our Father, you filled the heart of the Virgin Mary with your grace and made her the Mother of your Son and of the Church. By her prayers, make our hearts pure, open to your word and faithful in every trial, and gather the nations in peace. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, yesterday we looked at the Heart of Jesus; today we look at the Heart of his Mother. Simeon said to Mary: a sword will pierce your own soul too (Luke 2:35). The Heart of the Son and the heart of the Mother are joined in love and in suffering.

Her heart is called Immaculate because it was never stained by sin. God chose her before the foundation of the world to be holy and blameless in love (Ephesians 1:4), and preserved her from all sin from her conception, through the merits of Jesus, her Son and Saviour.

In the first reading God promises old Sarah a son, and Abraham laughs. But nothing is impossible with God. Sarah becomes the mother of a people; Mary becomes the Mother of all peoples, for Jesus gave her to us from the Cross: here is your mother.

Isaiah tells frightened King Ahaz: the Lord himself will give you a sign; the young woman shall bear a son, Immanuel. Saint Matthew sees it fulfilled in the Virgin Mary. Ahaz's heart was closed by fear; Mary's heart was open: here am I, the servant of the Lord (Luke 1:38).

In the Gospel Mary and Joseph search for the boy Jesus for three days in great anxiety. When they find him, they do not understand his words. But his mother treasured all these things in her heart (Luke 2:51). Mary did not understand everything, but she kept God's word and waited.

Parents, when you are worried about your children, bring them to Mary's heart. All of us, when God's ways are hard, let us keep his word as she did. And let us pray the rosary each day for peace, as she asked. Immaculate Heart of Mary, pray for us. Amen.
kids: Children, Mary and Joseph lost Jesus for three days, and they were very worried. When they found him, Mary kept everything in her heart.
Mary is our Mother too. When you are worried or sad, tell her: “Mother Mary, keep me in your heart.” And pray a Hail Mary for peace in the world!

intro: Theme: “His mother treasured all these things in her heart.”
On the Feast of the Immaculate Heart of Mary: Sarah, mother of nations; the sign of Immanuel; the Virgin chosen to be holy and blameless; and the heart that kept God's word in the dark.

q: I will bless her, and moreover I will give you a son by her. I will bless her, and she shall give rise to nations; kings of peoples shall come from her.
For nothing will be impossible with God.
points.apply: Entrust to God, through Mary, one situation that seems impossible.

points.h: The Lord himself will give you a sign
q: Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign. Look, the young woman is with child and shall bear a son, and shall name him Immanuel.
“Look, the virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and they shall name him Emmanuel,” which means, “God is with us.”
points.apply: When fear tempts you to close your heart this week, pray Mary's words: let it be with me according to your word.

points.h: Holy and blameless before him in love
sub: Chosen before the foundation of the world.
Preserved from sin by the blood of her Son.
q: You are altogether beautiful, my love; there is no flaw in you.
just as he chose us in Christ before the foundation of the world to be holy and blameless before him in love.
points.apply: Make a good confession soon, asking Mary to help you become what God chose you to be.

q: I treasure your word in my heart, so that I may not sin against you.
Then he went down with them and came to Nazareth, and was obedient to them. His mother treasured all these things in her heart.
points.apply: Each night this week, recall and keep one thing God did that day.

concl: The Immaculate Heart is God's masterpiece and our model: open to the word, faithful in anxiety, keeping what it does not yet understand.
As the apostles prayed with Mary, let us pray with her for the Spirit and for peace.
2027-06-05.resolve: This week, consecrate yourself to the Immaculate Heart, pray a decade of the rosary daily for peace, and treasure God's word each night.
